content.user_title: Identify Customer Jobs and Switching Motivations
content.value_statement: Requests for features or deliverables can hide the progress customers actually need. This skill uses Jobs to Be Done to clarify context, switching motivations, selection criteria, and next actions.
actual_capabilities: Translate solution requests into job statements connecting situation, desired progress, and expected outcomes.
Separate functional, emotional, and social jobs when they affect the current decision.
Analyze switching forces through push, pull, anxiety, and habit.
Extract three to five observable selection criteria with priorities and acceptable tradeoffs.
Adapt recommendations for product design, content, sales, personal decisions, or AI collaboration.
Rewrite prompts with context, constraints, deliverables, and acceptance criteria while labeling unsupported assumptions.
limitations: Conclusions depend on supplied evidence; missing motivations and behaviors remain hypotheses.
The skill provides analysis instructions, not automated interviews, analytics collection, or market validation.
JTBD does not replace user profiles, feature specifications, or ordinary task clarification.
The source prescribes Chinese writing conventions; other language requirements should be stated explicitly.

use_cases.title: Clarify product adoption barriers
use_cases.description: Turn customer notes into job hypotheses, switching forces, and prioritized selection criteria before proposing product changes.

use_cases.title: Align content with customer progress
use_cases.description: Connect audience situations, failed alternatives, desired outcomes, and credible evidence to a focused content brief.

use_cases.title: Improve AI task requests
use_cases.description: Rewrite a proposed deliverable around the underlying job, available materials, boundaries, and observable acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first job statement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs-jtbd for this request: [request]. Identify the situation, desired progress, and outcome. Mark missing evidence as hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze switching motivations
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these customer notes: [notes]. Identify functional, emotional, and social jobs. Explain push, pull, anxiety, and habit. Separate facts from assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare alternatives against criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Use JTBD to compare [alternatives] for [situation]. Derive three to five observable selection criteria. Prioritize requirements and tradeoffs. Propose one low-cost validation step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: support a product or service decision.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign an AI collaboration prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [original prompt] against [context and evidence]. Identify solution-job mismatches. Rewrite with constraints, deliverables, and acceptance criteria. State assumptions and one validation step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: align an AI workflow with the underlying job.

output_examples.input: Customers request a dashboard because preparing weekly updates requires copying figures from several spreadsheets.
output: Job hypothesis: Before the weekly meeting, consolidate figures into a reliable update so the team can make decisions.
Functional job: Prepare the update. Emotional job hypothesis: Reduce worry about missing figures. Social job hypothesis: Appear prepared.
Selection criteria: Traceable figures are required; reduced manual copying is preferred; acceptable setup effort needs confirmation.
Next step: Review one recent update process and test whether a consolidated report removes the main bottleneck.

output_examples.input: Rewrite my request for a launch article. We need existing customers to understand the changed workflow before Monday.
output: Job statement: When a workflow changes, customers need to understand the differences so they can continue their work on Monday.
Prompt: Draft a customer-facing launch article using [approved change notes]. Explain changed steps and preserve confirmed details.
Acceptance criteria: Identify affected users, describe each changed step, and distinguish confirmed information from missing details.
To confirm: Which customers are affected, and which workflow changes have been approved?

best_practices: Provide a concrete recent situation, the current alternative, and evidence of what failed.
Keep facts, inferred motivations, and unverified hypotheses clearly separated.
Use observable selection criteria and test the most consequential assumption with a low-cost action.
anti_patterns: Treating demographics, industry labels, or requested features as sufficient evidence of a customer job.
Inventing interview findings, behavior data, or motivations to complete the framework.
Forcing every request into JTBD or asking repeated broad questions when existing evidence is sufficient.

faq.question: What does JTBD mean here?
faq.answer: Jobs to Be Done describes the progress someone seeks in a specific situation and why they choose one solution over another.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. The package provides written guidance rather than executable integrations.

faq.question: Does it conduct customer research automatically?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes supplied materials and proposes hypotheses or validation steps. It does not collect interviews or behavioral analytics.

faq.question: What happens when information is missing?
faq.answer: It labels uncertain conclusions as hypotheses and asks one focused question only when missing information would change the recommendation.

faq.question: Can it help rewrite AI prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects the prompt to the underlying job and adds context, materials, boundaries, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Should I use it for every task?
faq.answer: No. Use it for customer choices, motivations, alternatives, or explicit JTBD prompt work. Ordinary acceptance-criteria clarification does not require this framework.
